summary.text: 桌 is the usual character for a table, desk, or stand. Its conventional analysis combines 木, which marks the furniture category, with 卓 as a sound element. The graph’s formation history is unsettled.

formation.text: The conventional analysis is phonosemantic: 木 contributes the furniture category, and 卓 supplies a sound cue. Some accounts suggest 卓’s sense “high” may have motivated the furniture name, but this does not establish how the graph was formed.

components.text: 木 is analyzed as the semantic element, marking the graph’s association with furniture such as a table or stand. No earlier form of this component within 桌 is identified.
卓 is conventionally analyzed as the sound element in 桌. Its own graph origin is unsettled; proposed accounts of its ancient shape do not establish how 桌 was formed.

sound.text: The modern Mandarin readings are close but have different tones.
The Baxter–Sagart table gives the same Middle Chinese form for 卓 and 桌.
The Baxter–Sagart table gives the same Old Chinese reconstruction for 卓 and 桌, while marking no pre-Qin examples for 桌.

history.text: No dated sequence of historical 桌 forms is established. The sources note that 桌 is absent from the cited Shuowen account, and no verified early graph shows how the present 木-plus-卓 analysis arose.

Historical reports cite 倚卓 for furniture in a passage associated with 998–1007, later Southern Song 棹 spellings, and a late-Ming dictionary gloss for 桌. These reports do not establish the earliest spelling or show that 桌 itself occurred in the early passage. The separate oar sense of 棹 does not establish a semantic link to furniture.

One account proposes that 卓’s lower 十 merged with or was replaced by 木, but the reported evidence does not support that graphic sequence. Other accounts describe 桌 as a 木-plus-卓 compound or as developing from an older 卓 form; neither is confirmed by a dated sequence of 桌 graphs.

uncertainties.text: The component analysis is conventional, but the graph’s formation remains unresolved: the evidence does not decide whether 木 was added to 卓, 桌 developed from an older 卓 form, or another graphic process produced it.
The reported early furniture term 倚卓/倚棹 is not evidence for a dated graph 桌. Its precise early witness, earliest spelling, and relation to 桌’s written form remain unresolved.
卓’s graph origin and proposed ancient pictorial interpretations remain unsettled and cannot establish 桌’s origin. No verified historical 桌 image or form sequence is available.

senses.text: 桌 names furniture such as a table, desk, or stand. Historical reports cite earlier furniture spellings, but do not show that 桌 itself was used in those early passages.

senses.gloss: a tableful; a table as a count of dishes or people
senses.text: A cited example uses 桌 as a classifier for a meal or for people counted by tables. Its date and development from the furniture noun are not established.

developments.text: The classifier use is attested, but its chronology and development from the furniture meaning are not established.

limitations.text: No pre-Qin graph or furniture use for 桌 is established. Reports of earlier furniture spellings do not identify the earliest attested spelling of the character itself.

overview.text: 桌 commonly means “table,” “desk,” or “stand.” In the conventional analysis, 木 marks the furniture category and 卓 provides a similar-sounding cue; the graph’s formation history remains unsettled.

components.text: 木 marks the furniture category in the conventional analysis.
卓 is the sound cue; its modern Mandarin reading is close to 桌’s, with a different tone.

relationships.text: The conventional analysis assigns 木 a furniture-related semantic contribution in 桌.

The conventional analysis identifies 卓 as the sound element. Their modern Mandarin readings are zhuó and zhuō; the cited Baxter–Sagart rows give matching Middle and Old Chinese forms, while the 桌 row notes no pre-Qin examples. These comparisons do not establish the graph’s date or formation history.

limitations.text: No verified image of 桌 or an identified historical form of 桌 is available to explain its graphic history. 卓 forms cannot stand in for 桌: the furniture word is reported in historical spellings 倚卓 and 倚棹, while available evidence does not establish a dated sequence showing how the graph 桌 arose. The proposed change from 卓 to 桌 by replacing or merging 十 with 木 remains unsupported.

evidence.text: Phonosemantic compound. 木 represents the meaning and 卓 represents the sound.

Ideogrammic compound (會意 /会意) and phono-semantic compound (形聲 /形声, OC *rteːwɢ): phonetic 卓 (OC *rteːwɢ, “high”) + semantic 木 (“tree; wood”) – table. The bottom 十 of 卓 has merged with or been replaced by 木. An obsolete variant that distinguishes the two components is 棹.
From 卓 (OC *rteːwɢ, “high”), as tables are relatively tall (compared to other pieces of furniture like 几 (OC *krilʔ, “stool”)).
Similar descriptive derivations for pieces of furniture include:
* 登 (OC *tɯːŋ, “to climb”) > 凳 (OC *tɯːŋs, “stool”)
* 倚 (OC *qralʔ, *qrals, “to lean”) > 椅 (OC *qral, *qralʔ, “chair”).

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫（Chinese University of Hong Kong）
evidence.text: Analyzes 桌 as 木 semantic plus 卓 phonetic, meaning a stand/table. Cites 正字通: “桌，呼几案曰桌.” Also cites an example from 兒女英雄傳, chapter 21, including 桌椅 and 一桌葷菜. The database describes 卓-derived “tall” as a possible motivation for the furniture name, but this is an account of the word’s naming, not proof that 桌 was first created by a semantic combination.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：桌

evidence.text: Describes the graph as 形聲, 从木、卓声; its detailed entry says “桌字本作『卓』” and reports later creation of 桌 with 木, also noting 棹 as a colloquial variant. The source does not provide primary evidence for when this graphic change occurred. Its account should therefore be treated as a dictionary explanation, not a securely dated formation history.
evidence.title: 桌 zhuō - 漢典

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫（Chinese University of Hong Kong）
evidence.text: States that 卓’s graph-form origin is unsettled. It reports bronze forms, Warring States Chu manuscript forms, and seal forms; the Shang-era Shuowen analysis reads it as “high” and explains the graph as 早 plus 匕. The database presents a competing proposal that it may depict a person standing at a height, and names 张世超’s interpretation of the lower portion as 昜. Its interpretation is explicitly tentative. Shuowen’s proposed form explanation should not be treated as confirmed palaeography.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：卓

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫（Chinese University of Hong Kong）
evidence.field: 卓—形義通解, citations to Shuowen and bronze inscriptions
evidence.text: Records 卓 in the Western Zhou Jiunian Weiding (九年衛鼎) and early Spring and Autumn Zhuo Linfu gui lid (卓林父簋蓋); it reports that the latter uses 卓 in the personal name 卓林父. Shuowen glosses the related headform 㔬 as 高也 (“high”). These early attestations establish the graph and an early personal-name use, not 桌 meaning furniture.
evidence.kind: dated inscription and historical dictionary report
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：卓

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫（Chinese University of Hong Kong）
evidence.field: 卓—形義通解, 桌-related discussion
evidence.text: Reports the competing historical account that furniture called 桌 was written 卓 (also 棹), citing 《正字通》 and 《蜀方言》, and quotes a proposal by Zhang Shenhui and Qiu Xigui that 桌 developed from an old form of 卓. It also quotes the explanation that 卓 supplied the “high” sense for a high stand. The source gives this as scholarly discussion rather than a demonstrated sequence of dated 桌 graph forms.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：卓

evidence.text: Treats 棹 as a variant of 桌 for the furniture sense, citing 正字通’s “倚棹”/“倚卓” spellings and a report from 楊億《談苑》 that檀香倚卓 were made in the 咸平、景德 reign periods (998–1007). It distinguishes this use from 棹/櫂 meaning oar, a separate character history. This is secondary reporting of an early furniture term, not evidence that the graph 桌 itself was present then.
evidence.title: 教育部《異體字字典》：A01921 桌

evidence.source: 雅昌专栏 / 澎湃新闻, 张辉, 《中国家具史》 column
evidence.text: Reports that the name is later than the furniture: 楊億《談苑》 is cited for “咸平景德中，主家造檀香倚卓” with an explanation that 卓然而高可倚; it reports Southern Song 棹 forms in 朱子語類 and 建炎以来系年要录, and says 卓 and 棹 were both used through Song, Yuan, and Ming. It identifies the late-Ming 正字通 wording “桌，俗呼几案曰桌” as the earliest dictionary record known to that author. These are reported textual attestations; this source does not reproduce manuscript witnesses or establish that no earlier occurrence exists.
evidence.title: 张辉：唐宋时期局脚桌流变——《中国家具史》

evidence.field: 棹—詳細解釋; 康熙字典; 音韻方言
evidence.text: Separately records 棹/櫂 as a phonosemantic graph 从木、卓声 with the early dictionary sense “long oar”; cites 楚辭《九歌·湘君》 “桂棹兮蘭枻.” It also records later boat/paddle senses and a distinct furniture reading/use “倚卓也,” citing 楊億《談苑》 for 檀香倚卓 in 998–1007. evidence.text: Records 卓 in the Western Zhou Jiunian Weiding (九年衛鼎) and early Spring and Autumn Zhuo Linfu gui lid (卓林父簋蓋); it reports that the latter uses 卓 in the personal name 卓林父. Shuowen glosses the related headform 㔬 as 高也 (“high”). These early attestations establish the graph and an early personal-name use, not 桌 meaning furniture.
evidence.kind: dated inscription and historical dictionary report
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：卓

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫（Chinese University of Hong Kong）
evidence.field: 卓—形義通解, 桌-related discussion
evidence.text: Reports the competing historical account that furniture called 桌 was written 卓 (also 棹), citing 《正字通》 and 《蜀方言》, and quotes a proposal by Zhang Shenhui and Qiu Xigui that 桌 developed from an old form of 卓. It also quotes the explanation that 卓 supplied the “high” sense for a high stand. The source gives this as scholarly discussion rather than a demonstrated sequence of dated 桌 graph forms.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：卓

evidence.text: Treats 棹 as a variant of 桌 for the furniture sense, citing 正字通’s “倚棹”/“倚卓” spellings and a report from 楊億《談苑》 that檀香倚卓 were made in the 咸平、景德 reign periods (998–1007). It distinguishes this use from 棹/櫂 meaning oar, a separate character history. This is secondary reporting of an early furniture term, not evidence that the graph 桌 itself was present then.
evidence.title: 教育部《異體字字典》：A01921 桌

evidence.source: 雅昌专栏 / 澎湃新闻, 张辉, 《中国家具史》 column
evidence.text: Reports that the name is later than the furniture: 楊億《談苑》 is cited for “咸平景德中，主家造檀香倚卓” with an explanation that 卓然而高可倚; it reports Southern Song 棹 forms in 朱子語類 and 建炎以来系年要录, and says 卓 and 棹 were both used through Song, Yuan, and Ming. It identifies the late-Ming 正字通 wording “桌，俗呼几案曰桌” as the earliest dictionary record known to that author. These are reported textual attestations; this source does not reproduce manuscript witnesses or establish that no earlier occurrence exists.
evidence.title: 张辉：唐宋时期局脚桌流变——《中国家具史》

evidence.field: 桌—康熙字典 quotation of 正字通
evidence.text: The entry quotes 正字通: “俗呼几案曰桌” (“tables/stands are colloquially called 桌”). Its cited wording documents a lexicographic characterization of the furniture sense; no publication date for the quoted 正字通 passage is supplied on this page.
evidence.title: 桌 zhuō - 漢典

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫（Chinese University of Hong Kong）
evidence.text: Records a later classifier use: 桌 can count meals or people by tables, with an example from 兒女英雄傳, chapter 21, “一桌葷菜.” The source supplies no date for this passage on the character page; the classifier development’s chronology therefore remains undetermined here.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：桌

evidence.field: 棹—詳細解釋; 康熙字典; 音韻方言
evidence.text: Separately records 棹/櫂 as a phonosemantic graph 从木、卓声 with the early dictionary sense “long oar”; cites 楚辭《九歌·湘君》 “桂棹兮蘭枻.” It also records later boat/paddle senses and a distinct furniture reading/use “倚卓也,” citing 楊億《談苑》 for 檀香倚卓 in 998–1007. The shared form and sound do not establish that the table word arose by borrowing the oar word or that one semantic development produced the other.
evidence.title: 棹 zhào、zhuō - 漢典

evidence.source: 中央研究院漢語多功能字庫
evidence.text: Reports Shuowen’s definition of 㔬/卓 as “high,” then cites early classical and later examples illustrating “standing out,” “surpassing,” and “tall.” This supports 卓’s independent semantic history; the furniture glosses of 卓/棹 are separately reported as historical spellings, so the senses should not be collapsed into one chronology.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：卓

context.provenance: Base evidence consists of imported local JSONL excerpts. Source names identify upstream datasets; extraction may lose sense and language boundaries. Further external evidence and research activity are documented separately in the dossier.
editorial_rules: Write about the character's graphic history; distinguish it from the history of a spoken word.
Separate historical explanation from mnemonics. Do not infer history from modern shapes or readings.
Sources may repeat one another. A source count is not independent corroboration.
Treat Shuowen as a historical account, not automatic confirmation. Its generated English glosses are excluded.
Unrelated word senses may appear in Wiktionary excerpts. Do not merge them into a character origin.
Related-character evidence retains its record_character. Do not silently transfer a traditional form's components to a simplified form.
No glyph image has been visually inspected in this packet. Do not claim to have inspected one.
Explain missing evidence explicitly, especially for Japanese-created characters. A Chinese spelling pronunciation is not evidence for a Japanese origin.

gaps: No pre-Qin examples for 桌 are reported in the local Baxter–Sagart row; available evidence does not establish a pre-Qin furniture sense or graph.

No independent pre-Qin attestation of 卓 used for furniture was verified. Reports place the related furniture term as 倚卓 in Yang Yi’s Song-era Tan Yuan (998–1007), with Southern Song 棹 spellings; exact original witnesses and earliest manuscript dates remain unchecked.

The claim that the 十 portion of 卓 merged with or was replaced by 木 is not established by the inspected sources. One dictionary says 桌 arose later with 木, but the historical form sequence and whether this was a graphic alteration, semantic differentiation, or folk/orthographic development remain unresolved.

The earliest-attested sequence of furniture senses is uncertain: accounts cite Song-period 倚卓/倚棹 but also state the graph 桌 is recorded by 正字通 in late Ming. A cited saying about the earliest dictionary entry is not a comprehensive corpus search.

The classifier sense ‘a tableful/one table of guests or dishes’ is attested in a cited novel example but its date and pathway from the furniture noun are not established in the inspected character-page evidence.

No 卓 Baxter–Sagart row was included in the provided local reading packet, and only the 桌 row was independently checked here. Do not infer 卓’s Baxter–Sagart form from 桌’s row or substitute Zhengzhang notation. Unicode U+5353 official record was attempted but failed to open.
The quoted pages list historical glyph images, but no glyph image was visually inspected. Graph-shape claims beyond page text and its cited reference listings remain unverified.
No source license or reuse grant was checked; no tracked source extract is recommended. Cite character-specific pages and use concise paraphrases.
No dated early form of the graph 桌 was established by the inspected pages. The early furniture word/orthography reported as 倚卓/倚棹 is separate evidence from the later dictionary entry 桌.

The reported semantic motivation ‘high’ from 卓 is a plausible naming account, but the evidence inspected does not prove that the word originated by combining 木 and 卓 or establish a precise graphic sequence. The claim that 卓’s 十 merged with or was replaced by 木 remains unsupported here.
No classifier-use chronology or proven pathway from table noun to a classifier was established.

The proposed original referent and original name/pronunciation of any object depicted by early 卓 forms remain unresolved; no such object-name premise is needed to support 卓 as a phonetic component in the later 桌 analysis.

The exact Unihan official URLs for 桌 and 卓 were attempted, but the live pages failed to open. Exact current Mandarin readings are reported from the provided local Unihan table rows; there is no external click-through verification in this run.

No source license or reuse grant for recurring dictionary text was checked; no local extract is recommended. Commons image rights apply to the modern vector files only, not to database or dictionary text.
No pre-Qin graph or furniture sense for 桌 is established by inspected sources. The local Baxter–Sagart row marks no pre-Qin examples; no external ancient 桌 witness was verified in this pass.

The reported 998–1007 倚卓 furniture term is not the same evidence as a dated graph 桌. Its exact manuscript witness and earliest spelling remain unverified; secondary sources report later Southern Song 棹 forms and a Ming-era 桌 dictionary entry.

Accounts differ over whether 桌 arose by adding semantic 木 to 卓, derived from an older 卓 form, or developed through vernacular orthography. The proposed merging/replacement of 卓’s 十 by 木 is not supported by the sources inspected.

Current Mandarin rows supplied locally are 卓 zhuó, 桌 zhuō, 棹 zhào. Baxter–Sagart exact local rows are 卓 MC traewk, OC *tˤrawk and 桌 MC traewk, OC *tˤrawk (no pre-Qín exx.); these are local data, not ancient proof of the component role. Unicode official records for 卓 and 桌 were not successfully inspected in this run, so no external click-through evidence is added for those local readings.
The classifier sense for dishes/guests is present in cited novel examples, but the date of its earliest use and its pathway from the furniture noun are not established here.

No glyph image is proposed. Available 卓 Commons image candidates returned 404 at acquisition; the official Xiaoxuetang query for 桌 returned 401, and the ZDIC old-script index did not establish a 桌 image. Thus no alternative image with verified identity and rights was established.

limitations.text: No verified image of 桌 or an identified historical form of 桌 is available to explain its graphic history. 卓 forms cannot stand in for 桌: the furniture word is reported in historical spellings 倚卓 and 倚棹, while available evidence does not establish a dated sequence showing how the graph 桌 arose. The proposed change from 卓 to 桌 by replacing or merging 十 with 木 remains unsupported.
